prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with wrist fracture after a side impact at intersection. The patient had 13 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1154; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Some exam findings support the injury; other tests are normal.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
text: Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection, sustaining a distal radius fracture consistent with the mechanism and force of the crash. Over the course of thirteen visits, treatment proceeded along a typical recovery pathway: immobilization, followed by progressive range-of-motion and strengthening exercises, with visit frequency tapering as symptoms and function improved. Examination findings include localized tenderness and reduced grip strength on the affected side that support the fracture diagnosis, while neurovascular testing and the remaining orthopedic maneuvers were within normal limits. Review of the record shows the patient received care for the same wrist region within the preceding two years, and that prior condition appears to contribute to some of the current complaints. Billing records were reviewed and reflect single charges for each service rendered, with no duplicated entries. Continued home exercise and follow-up as needed are recommended.
